venue_now: ECAI 2025, per the arXiv comment 'Accepted at ECAI 2025' on 2509.04013v1 (notes/arxiv_abs_check.json)
what_it_is: A study of how paraphrasing benchmark questions changes LLM scores and rankings (p.1). GPT-4o mini wrote five paraphrases of each of 53,966 questions from six multiple-choice benchmarks (ARC-C, HellaSwag, MMLU, OpenBookQA, RACE, SciQ), under a prompt asking it to preserve meaning; 31 questions it refused were dropped (p.3-4). Thirty-four LLMs answer the originals and the paraphrases in a four-option format (p.3-4). Absolute accuracy drops significantly, while Kendall's tau between the rankings on original and median paraphrased accuracy is above 0.9 on every benchmark (p.1, p.6-7).
domain: general knowledge and commonsense multiple-choice benchmarks
size: 53,966 questions from six benchmarks, five paraphrases each; 34 models (p.3-4)
evaluation: four-option accuracy, consistency across paraphrases, Kendall's tau between rankings (p.4-7)
human_validation: none reported for the paraphrases: meaning preservation rests on the prompt's instructions (p.4)
contamination_measures: paraphrases as a probe of wording dependence

engtrace_use.sentence: ... randomly sampled variants can overstate robustness [@mondorf2026lpds], and paraphrasing lowers absolute scores while leaving model rankings relatively stable [@lunardi2025paraphraserobustness].
engtrace_use.explanation: This is the paper's own summary (p.1, p.7), but it is a finding on six multiple-choice benchmarks with unchecked LLM paraphrases (p.3-4), and the sentence states it as a general fact. EngTrace's own arm does not reproduce it, on either count: no model's paraphrase difference is significant after Holm (between -3.1 and +1.6 points; ten of eleven within 5 points at 90%), and the agreement between the two orderings, tau 0.636, sits at the 5th percentile of the noise distribution at the arm's size (full_run_28092026/PARAPHRASE_PAPER_NOTES.md). Scoping the clause to multiple-choice benchmarks avoids a contradiction a reader would otherwise see.

suggested_wording: ... and on multiple-choice benchmarks paraphrasing lowers absolute scores while leaving model rankings relatively stable [@lunardi2025paraphraserobustness].
facts_to_cite: six multiple-choice benchmarks, 53,966 questions, five GPT-4o mini paraphrases each, 34 LLMs (p.3-4)
rankings remain relatively stable while absolute effectiveness declines significantly (p.1)
Kendall's tau between original and median paraphrased rankings above 0.9 on every benchmark (p.6-7)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: paraphrases as a test of whether scores depend on the wording. Differs: EngTrace's paraphrases keep every number, unit and symbol, are script-checked and then confirmed by an own-branch expert, who rejected 12% of those passing the scripts, mostly for a dropped qualifier that changes the problem (PARAPHRASE_PAPER_NOTES.md item 7); Lunardi's are unchecked. The two results should be set side by side only within the notes' rules: not 'robust to paraphrasing', not 'the ranking is stable', and not 'no contamination' for EngTrace. A fair contrast for the robustness section: on multiple-choice benchmarks with unchecked paraphrases, scores drop and rankings hold (tau above 0.9); on EngTrace's expert-checked paraphrases, no drop survives correction and the tiers hold but the order within the top tier is not resolved.
notes: (1) Nothing in v3 may imply that EngTrace's ranking is stable under rewording; the sentence is about this paper and stays so. (2) The paper's own caution (its benchmarks are multiple choice; open-ended sets like GSM8K were excluded, p.3) supports scoping the clause.
